uncited: Empirical and Hybrid Models provide non-physical or semi-physical approximations for volumetric light transport, prioritizing visual fidelity and performance over strict adherence to the Radiative Transfer Equation (RTE).

Unlike physically accurate methods that solve for multiple scattering, these models use heuristic shading terms, blurred indirect light, or hybrid surface-volume compositing to simulate translucency and atmospheric effects at interactive rates.

They set themselves apart from [Absorption-only model](839-absorption-only-model.md) by including scattering-like effects, and from [Single Scattering Model](1053-single-scattering-model.md) by avoiding the computational cost of exact integration, often relying on precomputed gradients or empirical blur operations.
The family shares a reliance on approximating the complex integral of the RTE through simplified shading functions or hybrid rendering pipelines.
The concepts stem from the need for real-time or near-real-time visualization of complex volumetric data, such as medical imaging (e.g., zebrafish embryos, brain tumors) and CFD simulations.
